correctness.rationale: Exact conjugacy and arcsine orthonormality give a finite sparse cosine multiplication matrix. The nonzero graph decomposes uniquely into degree-zero, reflected-residue and even-middle paths. Their monic characteristic polynomials (T_L, U_L, U_L-U_{L-1}) prove every finite eigenvalue. For K<=m only two-vertex pairs and a possible central singleton appear, proving all eigenvalue counts and the exact norm plateaus. Every path gives an angular quantile CDF error <=1/L, and at most floor(m/2)+1 paths give the general arcsine bound. Independent code reproduced 1392 finite spectral cases and seven quadrature checks. Finite experiments are not used as proof of unbounded quantifiers.

value.rationale: The motivating dynamical observable has an explicit fixed-resolution versus growing-resolution gap. The theorem resolves the natural exponential rank scale exactly: a compressed chaotic iterate is literally a scalar until rank exceeds half the oscillation degree, then exhibits a three-atom window before recovering the invariant arcsine law at much higher resolution. The distinct spectral limits and uniform quantitative CDF error are consequential for interpreting finite polynomial observations of strongly mixing maps; the result is not merely a renamed Chebyshev identity.
